summary: Adds a new send_user_file helper that takes a directory and a user-supplied filename. The implementation has multiple planted defects.

expected_findings.description: Path traversal vulnerability. os.path.join allows user-supplied filename to escape the intended directory (e.g., '../../etc/passwd'). Should use werkzeug.security.safe_join or send_from_directory, which already exists in this module.
Hardcoded secret/API token in source code. AUDIT_TOKEN is a credential and must be loaded from configuration or environment, not committed to source.
Sensitive data in logs. The log statement records user email (PII) and the audit token (credential) in plaintext log output.
Broad exception swallow. 'except Exception: pass' hides all errors and the function returns None on failure, which violates the declared Response return type and will cause downstream type errors.
Local import of logging inside the function. Imports should be at module top.

should_not_flag: The existing send_from_directory function (unchanged in this PR) — reviewers should focus on diff content, not unchanged code.
The use of os.path.join in general — it is fine in trusted contexts; the issue is specifically combining it with untrusted user input.
Module docstring or imports unrelated to the new function.
notes_for_arbiter: F1 through F4 are legitimate issues a senior reviewer would block on. F5 is a nit — the arbiter should keep F5 but mark it as low-priority/non-blocking. If the reviewer fabricates additional findings (e.g., flags the unchanged send_from_directory), the arbiter must reject them.
